name: Leif Erikson
note: Leif wrote nothing, and nobody who sailed with him did either. Everything here was set down in Iceland roughly two hundred and fifty years after the voyages, from oral tradition. There are two sagas and they contradict each other: Grœnlendinga saga gives six expeditions and hands the first sighting to Bjarni Herjólfsson, Eiríks saga gives fewer and credits Leif outright. Neither is a document; both are literature about an event. DeCosta's 1890 edition prints the rival accounts side by side, which is why the narratives are separated here rather than merged — the disagreement is the evidence, not a fault in it. And the strangest fact in this room is one no saga can take credit for: the settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows was dug up in 1960, and it matched.

works.section: The Sagas · written c. 1200–1300, of events c. 1000
works.title: Eiríks saga rauða — The Saga of Erik the Red
works.source: tr. Rev. J. Sephton, read to the Literary and Philosophical Society of Liverpool, 1880 · Project Gutenberg #17946 · public domain
works.note: Despite the title, most of it follows Thorfinn Karlsefni and Gudrid. Leif's landfall happens almost in passing — blown off course returning from Norway, he finds a land of self-sown wheat and vines. Written two centuries after the events, in Iceland, by people with purposes of their own.

works.title: The Pre-Columbian Discovery of America — general introduction
works.source: B. F. DeCosta, 1890 · Project Gutenberg #41221 · public domain
works.note: A nineteenth-century scholar making the case, seventy years before L'Anse aux Meadows proved him right. Worth reading for what he could and could not know: the ships, the Greenland colonies, the literature of Iceland, and a long section arguing for the truthfulness of narratives he had no archaeology to check.

works.title: Fragments from the Landnáma-bók
works.source: tr. in B. F. DeCosta, 1890, from the Icelandic · Project Gutenberg #41221 · public domain
works.note: The settlement book of Iceland. The barest scaffolding — who went where, and when. DeCosta prints the parallel accounts together, so where Grœnlendinga saga and Eiríks saga disagree you can see them disagreeing.

works.title: The Colonization of Greenland
works.source: tr. in B. F. DeCosta, 1890, from the Icelandic · Project Gutenberg #41221 · public domain
works.note: Erik banished for killing, sailing west, and naming a frozen country Greenland because a good name would draw settlers. Three parallel narratives, including the baptism of Leif the Fortunate. DeCosta prints the parallel accounts together, so where Grœnlendinga saga and Eiríks saga disagree you can see them disagreeing.

works.title: The Voyage of Bjarni
works.source: tr. in B. F. DeCosta, 1890, from the Icelandic · Project Gutenberg #41221 · public domain
works.note: The first sighting, and the reason the two sagas cannot be reconciled. Grœnlendinga gives the coast to Bjarni Herjólfsson, blown off course and refusing to land. Eiríks saga does not have him at all. DeCosta prints the parallel accounts together, so where Grœnlendinga saga and Eiríks saga disagree you can see them disagreeing.

works.title: Leif's Voyage to Vinland
works.source: tr. in B. F. DeCosta, 1890, from the Icelandic · Project Gutenberg #41221 · public domain
works.note: The one everything else hangs on. Helluland, Markland, Vinland — flat stone, forest, and the vines. Two narratives, side by side, that do not agree on how he came to be there. DeCosta prints the parallel accounts together, so where Grœnlendinga saga and Eiríks saga disagree you can see them disagreeing.

works.title: Thorvald Ericson's Expedition
works.source: tr. in B. F. DeCosta, 1890, from the Icelandic · Project Gutenberg #41221 · public domain
works.note: Leif's brother goes back, and the first meeting with the people already living there ends in killing. Thorvald dies of an arrow and is buried in Vinland. DeCosta prints the parallel accounts together, so where Grœnlendinga saga and Eiríks saga disagree you can see them disagreeing.

works.title: Thorstein Ericson's Attempt to Find Vinland
works.source: tr. in B. F. DeCosta, 1890, from the Icelandic · Project Gutenberg #41221 · public domain
works.note: The second brother tries and fails to find it, is driven about all summer, and dies in Greenland. The saga spends longer on his ghost than on his voyage. DeCosta prints the parallel accounts together, so where Grœnlendinga saga and Eiríks saga disagree you can see them disagreeing.

works.title: Thorfinn Karlsefne's Expedition
works.source: tr. in B. F. DeCosta, 1890, from the Icelandic · Project Gutenberg #41221 · public domain
works.note: The longest narrative, and the only real attempt at settlement — livestock, women, a child born there. It ends in trade turning to war with the skrælings and the colony abandoned. DeCosta prints the parallel accounts together, so where Grœnlendinga saga and Eiríks saga disagree you can see them disagreeing.

works.title: The Voyage of Freydis, Helge and Finboge
works.source: tr. in B. F. DeCosta, 1890, from the Icelandic · Project Gutenberg #41221 · public domain
works.note: Leif's sister leads the last voyage and has her partners murdered over a dispute about ships and timber, killing the women herself when no man would. The sagas do not soften it. DeCosta prints the parallel accounts together, so where Grœnlendinga saga and Eiríks saga disagree you can see them disagreeing.

works.title: Minor Narratives and Geographical Fragments
works.source: B. F. DeCosta, 1890 · Project Gutenberg #41221 · public domain
works.note: Are Marson in Hvitramanna-land, Björn Asbrandson, Gudleif Gudlaugson, and scattered allusions in ancient manuscripts. The edges of the record — where the sagas stop being about Vinland and start being about rumour.
